subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack OAuth token rotation in the Slack plugin now, and where should client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and adopted at runtime?
rationale: This changes credential persistence and live auth behavior for a workspace integration, so automation cannot safely choose the security model, config shape, or recovery UX.

options.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Implement token rotation inside the Slack plugin with secure storage, transactional refresh-token replacement, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof while preserving static-token setups.

options.title: Keep external rotation for now
options.body: Leave OpenClaw on static Slack tokens and document the external rotation/manual operational path until maintainers are ready to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Wait for shared credential-refresh seam
options.body: Defer Slack-specific work until OpenClaw has a generic plugin credential refresh/storage API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Implement token rotation inside the Slack plugin with secure storage, transactional refresh-token replacement, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof while preserving static-token setups.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest broad Slack plugin/runtime routing signal and can coordinate the security/product decision with current config owners.
